Brown-McLean syndrome is a form of aphakic bullous keratopathy, characterized by peripheral corneal edema and guttata in aphakic eyes, often with central sparing. The clinical findings (aphakia, peripheral microcystic corneal edema with central sparing, central corneal guttata, Scheimpflug findings) are highly consistent with Brown-McLean syndrome.
